title: Circuit and Last-Mile Link Utilization Monitoring
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Circuit and Last-Mile Link Utilization Monitoring' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_circuit_and_last_mile_link_utilization_monitorin` (UC-5.10.8), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Circuit and Last-Mile Link Utilization Monitoring", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=network` sourcetype='snmp:interface' that satisfy the UC-5.10.8 SPL filters for 'Circuit and Last-Mile Link Utilization Monitoring'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `network` / `snmp:interface` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `operational_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-5.10.8.

dataSources: `index=network sourcetype=snmp:interface` polling IF-MIB/high-capacity counters (`ifHCInOctets`, `ifHCOutOctets`, `ifSpeed`, `ifDescr`, `ifAdminStatus`, `ifOperStatus`) from PE/CPE routers facing carrier tail circuits; optionally merge `carrier_circuits.csv` supplying committed information rate (CIR), location, and carrier circuit ID. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: SNMP Modular Input or Telegraf SNMP plugin feeding Splunk; optional `TA-cisco_ios`/`Splunk_TA_juniper` for enrichment macros. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=network sourcetype="snmp:interface" ifSpeed>0 ifDescr=*
| sort 0 host, ifDescr, _time
| streamstats current=f global=f last(ifHCInOctets) as prev_in last(ifHCOutOctets) as prev_out last(_time) as prev_ts by host, ifDescr
| eval dt=_time-prev_ts
| eval in_bps=if(dt>0 AND dt<900,(ifHCInOctets-prev_in)*8/dt,null())
| eval out_bps=if(dt>0 AND dt<900,(ifHCOutOctets-prev_out)*8/dt,null())
| eval speed_bps=case(ifSpeed>=4294967295 AND isnotnull(ifHighSpeed), ifHighSpeed*1000000, ifSpeed>=4294967295, null(), true(), ifSpeed)
| eval util_peak=if(isnotnull(speed_bps) AND speed_bps>0, round(100*max(in_bps,out_bps)/speed_bps,2), null())
| eval host_interface=host."|".ifDescr
| lookup carrier_circuits.csv host_interface OUTPUT cir_bps carrier circuit_id site_code
| eval cir_util=if(isnotnull(cir_bps) AND cir_bps>0, round(100*max(in_bps,out_bps)/cir_bps,2), null())
| where util_peak>75 OR cir_util>85
| stats latest(util_peak) as snmp_util_pct latest(cir_util) as cir_util_pct latest(ifOperStatus) as oper latest(ifDescr) as interface by host, carrier, circuit_id
| sort -cir_util_pct
description: Turns IF-MIB counter deltas into sustained bits-per-second utilization on carrier-facing interfaces and overlays contractual CIR utilization so operations sees both physical port saturation and committed-rate overrun risk on tail circuits.
value: Capacity planners receive empirical trending ahead of billable overage or congestion-driven SLA breaches—especially valuable where uplinks remain physically uncapped but billing meters enforce CIR envelopes enforced only on carrier side.
implementation: Poll five-minute intervals minimum; align clocks via NTP; maintain lookup tying Splunk `host`/SNMP index to commercial circuit metadata; alert dual thresholds—SNMP physical utilization above seventy-five percent and CIR utilization above eighty-five percent.
visualization: Gauge tiles per circuit for instantaneous utilization; dual-axis timechart comparing SNMP utilization vs CIR utilization; map panel keyed by site_code with color thresholds.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'Circuit and Last-Mile Link Utilization Monitoring'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `network` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `operational_exceptions.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Reliable IF-MIB polling every five minutes (or faster for bursty tails) using `ifHCInOctets`/`ifHCOutOctets` on carrier-facing interfaces; legacy 32-bit counters require exclusion.
• Verified `ifSpeed` plus optional `ifHighSpeed` when ports exceed four-gigabit semantic limits—maintain override CSV when optics negotiate unexpected speeds.
• Carrier contract artifacts defining CIR in bits per second per VLAN or physical interface; finance-approved conversions when framing overhead differs.
• Network Time Protocol discipline across SNMP agents and Splunk indexers to prevent negative deltas.

Step 1 — Land telemetry as `sourcetype=snmp:interface` inside `index=network`, ensuring hosts resolve to the same identifiers used in inventory tools.

Step 2 — Chronologically sort per `host`/`ifDescr`, then apply `streamstats` deltas transforming octet growth into sustained throughput (multiply by eight, divide by elapsed seconds).

Step 3 — Compose `host_interface` keys (`host|ifDescr`) feeding `carrier_circuits.csv` so Splunk enriches circuits with carrier names, POP/site codes, billing IDs, and CIR.

Step 4 — Dashboard row displays SNMP-derived physical utilization beside CIR-relative utilization; schedule alerts crossing seventy-five percent physical or eighty-five percent CIR with staggered severities.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting: SNMP timeouts yield bogus spikes—drop intervals lacking sequential samples; EtherChannel members may need aggregated counters via vendor-specific MIB supplements; DSL tails remain asymmetric—consider direction-specific thresholds instead of `max()`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (SNMP Modular Input or Telegraf SNMP plugin feeding Splunk; optional `TA-cisco_ios`/`Splunk_TA_juniper` for enrichment macros. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=snmp:interface into network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`carrier, cir_bps, cir_bps carrier circuit_id site_code, cir_util`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how full the pipe is between us and the phone company so we upgrade or reshuffle traffic before everything slows to a crawl at rush hour.
